# device

`capability`, `connection`, `identity`, `registry`, and `discovery` define the controller-device discovery boundary, covering hardware classification, transport bindings, capability masks, stable identifiers, registry synchronization, and diagnostic formatting.

## Contents

### Capability

- [capability.hpp](./capability.hpp) defines `capability`, `capabilities`, capability bit values, mask operations, and comparison/composition operators.
- [capability.cpp](./capability.cpp) defines `operator<<(ostream&, capabilities)` for ordered diagnostic serialization.

### Identity and Transport

- [identity.hpp](./identity.hpp) defines `vendor_id`, `product_id`, `family`, known Sony and Microsoft identifiers, `device_identity`, and `classify`.
- [identity.cpp](./identity.cpp) defines `to_string(family)`, `operator<<(ostream&, family)`, and USB identity classification.
- [connection.hpp](./connection.hpp) defines `xinput_binding`, `hid_binding`, `transport_binding`, `same_binding`, and `device_connection`.
- [connection.cpp](./connection.cpp) compares `transport_binding` physical identities.

### Identifiers

- [id.hpp](./id.hpp) defines `device_id`, `no_device`, `transport_kind`, `connection`, `user_index`, and `report_id`.
- [id.cpp](./id.cpp) defines diagnostic formatting for `device_id`, `transport_kind`, and `connection`.

### Registry and Discovery

- [registry.hpp](./registry.hpp) defines the thread-safe `registry` API, stable ID allocation, and membership `generation`.
- [registry.cpp](./registry.cpp) implements registry insertion, refresh, removal, lookup, iteration, synchronization, and context reporting.
- [discovery.hpp](./discovery.hpp) defines interval-gated `discovery` reconciliation and its 1-second `interval`.
- [discovery.cpp](./discovery.cpp) implements XInput/HID scanning, capability classification, registration, notification handling, and departure cleanup.

## Architecture / Data Flow

`discovery::scan()` consumes `notifier_` state and clock values, invokes `scan_now()` when required, and reconciles `registry` membership.

`discovery::scan_now()` collects `transport_binding` values, scans XInput first, conditionally scans HID, and passes unseen bindings to `retire_unseen()`.

`registry::add()` deduplicates through `same_binding()`, refreshes existing `device_connection` facts, or assigns a monotonic `device_id`; `registry::remove()` retires departed devices.

`device_identity` selects `family`, `capabilities_for()` records factual hardware support, and drivers outside `device` decode reports and emit samples.

## Behavioral Contracts

- `operator<<(ostream&, capabilities)` emits `{}` or ordered names: `gyroscope`, `accelerometer`, `touchpad`, `battery`, `microphone-button`, `back-buttons`, `rumble`, `haptics`, `adaptive-triggers`, `light-bar`, `player-leds`.
- `capabilities::has(capability c)` requires all queried bits and returns `false` for `capability::none`.
- `user_index::try_from(int)` returns `nullopt` for `v < 0 || v >= count`; valid slots are `[0, 4)`.
- `same_binding()` compares `xinput_binding::index` or `hid_binding::path`; differing alternatives and `std::monostate` return `false`.
- `classify()` checks `product_dualsense_edge` before `product_dualsense`, gates HID recognition with `vendor_sony`, and returns `family::unknown` for unsupported pairs.
- `scan_hid()` requires `e.link != connection::unknown`; `scan_xinput()` records `connection::unknown`.
- `registry::for_each()` invokes callbacks while holding `mutex_`; callbacks must not call `add`, `remove`, `find`, or `size`.
- `generation_` increments only for membership insertion and removal; binding refreshes leave `generation_` unchanged.
- `static_assert(sizeof(report_id) == 1)` preserves `report_id` wire representation.
- `connection` values describe report framing, while `transport_kind` values describe delivery mechanisms.

## Capability Classification

`capabilities_for(family::xbox)` returns `capability::rumble`.

`capabilities_for(family::dualshock4)` returns gyroscope, accelerometer, touchpad, battery, rumble, and light-bar capabilities.

`capabilities_for(family::dualsense)` returns `dualsense_capabilities`; `family::dualsense_edge` adds `capability::back_buttons`.

`capabilities_for(family::unknown)` returns empty `capabilities`.

## File Relationships

`discovery.cpp` composes `transport_binding`, `device_identity`, `capabilities`, `connection`, and `registry`.

`registry.cpp` depends on `device_connection` and `same_binding()` to preserve stable records across repeated scans.

`id.cpp`, `identity.cpp`, and `capability.cpp` implement stream and string functions declared by `id.hpp`, `identity.hpp`, and `capability.hpp`.
